title: Desk Guide — Donation of Capital Credit Payouts and Patronage Tax Reporting
content:
# Donation of Payouts and Patronage Tax Reporting

**Capital Credits (Patronage Capital), every patron class.**

## Donation elections

Where the class allows donation (every class does), a member may elect that future payouts be donated to one of the accepted recipients — Operation Round Up or the Scholarship Fund — or cancel the election.

- The election applies to payouts made after it is recorded and is never applied retroactively to a payout already made.
- A donated payout is a payout by donation and pays nothing to the member.
- An estate's payout is never donated without the claimant's own election on the estate application.

| Election recorded | Payout date | Payout donated |
|---|---|---|
| Operation Round Up, recorded March 4 | December 10 of the same year | Yes |
| Scholarship Fund, recorded December 15 | December 10 of the same year | No — the payout was made before the election |
| Election cancelled, recorded June 2 | December 10 of the same year | No |

## Form 1099-PATR reporting

Payouts to a class that reports on IRS Form 1099-PATR — the Farm, General Service, Irrigation and Large Power Patron Classes — are reported on Form 1099-PATR when the member's calendar-year payouts reach $10.00.

## Backup withholding

Backup withholding of 24 percent is taken from a reportable payout only when no taxpayer identification number is on file. Where a taxpayer identification number is on file, no backup withholding is taken.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A General Service Patron Class member is paid $120.00 in one calendar year with no taxpayer identification number on file. The payout is reportable, and 24 percent of it, $28.80, is withheld. Had a taxpayer identification number been on file, nothing would have been withheld.
